description.summary: A creature from American lumberjack folklore that always hides behind trees or objects, never seen directly. Said to stalk lumberjacks and always stay behind them, moving when they move.
description.full: The Hidebehind is a fearsome critter from American lumberjack folklore, notable for being impossible to see directly. According to the tall tales, it always positions itself behind the nearest tree or object, perpetually staying out of view. When a lumberjack turns around, it instantly moves to stay behind them. This creature was used to explain the disappearances of lumberjacks who wandered into the woods alone and the paranoid feeling of being watched in the forest. It served as both entertainment for lumber camps and a cautionary tale for inexperienced workers (greenhorns) about the dangers of wandering off alone.

history.modern_era: The Hidebehind has seen renewed interest through its inclusion in the Fantastic Beasts film franchise and continued appreciation of American folklore. It remains a memorable example of lumberjack humor and tall tale tradition.

stories: Tales of the paranoid feeling of being watched in forests
folklore.beliefs: Never taken seriously; understood as humorous tall tale and cautionary fiction

purpose.entertainment: Told around lumber camp fires for amusement
purpose.safety: Discouraged workers from wandering into dangerous forest areas alone
purpose.explanation: Provided humorous explanation for genuine dangers (getting lost, wildlife, accidents)
